starting-out.speaker: Cook
starting-out.text: How is the adventuring going, my friend?

options.text: Do you have any other quests for me?

steps.player: Do you have any other quests for me? That last one of yours was so much fun, I was hoping you would!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ooooh dear, I might have, but it's all very embarrassing...

steps.player: Embarrassing? How do you mean?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Weeellll... You know I told you that it was the Duke's birthday?

steps.player: Yup, that's why I had to go and collect you things to make a cake with wasn't it?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yeeeesssss... Weeeelllll...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: It isn't. I don't even know when his birthday is!

steps.prompt: How does that make you feel?

steps.player: GRRRR! Why did you have me running around finding ingredients for you then?!?!

options.text: I don't really care to be honest.

steps.player: So you lied to me to get me to do you a favour?
Fair enough, you're not the first, but why lie? You could have just asked me, I'd have been happy to help.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I needed to test you and see if I could trust you...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I am in a terrible pickle, and I desperately need somebody trustworthy to help me out!

options.text: What seems to be the problem?

steps.player: You need help AGAIN? Well, what seems to be the problem?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, you're obviously trustworthy, I guess I could tell you...

steps.player: Please do. The suffering of others always seems to turn out very profitable for me.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well... It's like this...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you ever hear of Franizzard Van Lumbcook?

steps.player: Erm... Can't say I have.
And with a name like that, I'm sure I would remember.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, he was a great chef, and also my ancestor.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: One hundred years ago there was a very important meeting held here in Lumbridge Castle, and he cooked a banquet for the meeting, which was so stupendously amazing that he was offered a job for life, along with all

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: of his descendants.

steps.player: So you have your job because a hundred years ago your ancestor was a very good cook.
I don't see how that's much of a problem for you...
In fact I would say you are a VERY LUCKY man indeed. Frankly, I'd have fired you by now if you worked for me.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oooooh no.... You don't understand...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: This big important secret meeting that Franizzard cooked for is held here in Lumbridge castle every 10 years, and tonight will be the tenth anniversary of it!

steps.player: Still not seeing the problem...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, I have always felt like a failure as a cook, and that my job here is down to the skills of my ancestor.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I want to prove to the world that I am a great cook too!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: But to do that... (sigh) No, it just won't work...

steps.player: What won't? Come on man, pull yourself together and speak to me!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: (sniff) Weeeeelll... I thought that I would recreate the meal Franizzard cooked all of those years ago, the one that impressed

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: everybody so much... There's just this small problem though...

steps.player: Let me take a wild guess: You have the recipe but you don't have any of the ingredients, and OBVIOUSLY you can't just go and get them yourself?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yes! However did you know?

steps.player: Call it a hunch.
Okay, tell me what you're after and then I'll decide if I want to help you or not.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, they are common enough ingredients, although I must admit the recipe I am following is very strange indeed...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I will pay you upfront for any expenses you may incur while obtaining them, and of course you may keep the change for being so helpful to me.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Please can you help me? The feast is scheduled to start very soon, and I simply cannot leave!

steps.prompt: Start the Recipe for Disaster quest?

steps.player: I would love to help you! What do I have to do?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, I have an incredibly important banquet that I have to prepare for, and I am using an ancient cookbook to recreate the meal my famous ancestor made a hundred years ago.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Most of the ingredients I was able to obtain fairly easily, but there were some... oddities... that I have been unable to lay my hands on.

steps.player: Like what?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I need the following ingredients as soon as possible!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: One Eye Of NewtA freshly made 'Dirty Blast'A rotten tomato

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: And a glass of greenman's ale.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I have given you 100 coins to cover any expenses you may incur, feel free to keep the change.

steps.player: I'll go look for those for you then!
To be honest... I just can't be bothered.
Sorry about that.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh nooooo... What am I going to do now?

steps.player: Dunno. Maybe I'll change my mind and come back later and help you.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oooohhh... I really hope you do...

options.text: No thanks, I don't want to help.

steps.player: You know... Thinking about it...
I just can't be bothered to help you out. You'll have to find some other adventurer to do your little quest for you.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I guess I don't have anything more to say to you then.

steps.player: I guess you don't.

options.text: How do you still have a job?

steps.player: I'm curious... How exactly do you still have a job?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'm sorry? How do you mean?

steps.player: It's just surprising that you would still have employment as head cook of Lumbridge castle, given how obviously bad at your job you are.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: WHAT?

steps.player: Well, things you would expect every kitchen to have... Eggs, milk, flour... You know... But you don't.
And what is worse, you don't even go off and get them yourself, you expect people like me to run around after you!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I know I'm such a failure... I bring shame to my honourable ancestor, and now I need help again...

steps.player: Help again?
You need help AGAIN? Well, what seems to be the problem?

options.text: I am getting strong and mighty.

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.player: About those ingredients you wanted for the banquet...

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.text: Did you bring them? Remember, I need an eye of newt, a glass of greenman's ale, a rotten tomato, and a 'Dirty Blast'!
If the player has none of the ingredients:

steps.player: Erm... Sorry, I don't have any of that with me...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well come back when you have all of them! And hurry! It is a VERY important meeting!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-without-all-o.text: If the player has some of the ingredients:

steps.player: Weeelll... I have some of that stuff with me, but not all of it...

steps.text: If the player has only one of the ingredients:

steps.player: I'm afraid I only have [a/an] [item name] with me...

steps.text: If the player has only two of the ingredients:

steps.player: I'm afraid I only have [a/an] [item 1] and [a/an] [item 2] with me...

steps.text: If the player is missing only the eye of newt:

steps.player: I've got a 'Dirty Blast', a Greenman's ale and a rotten tomato, I just need to get the eye of newt!

steps.text: If the player is missing only the rotten tomato:

steps.player: I've got the 'Dirty Blast', a Greenman's ale and the eye of newt, I just have to find myself a rotten tomato...

steps.text: If the player is missing only the greenman's ale:

steps.player: I managed to find a 'Dirty Blast', a rotten tomato and an eye of newt, but I didn't manage to get a hold of a Greenman's ale yet...

steps.text: If the player is missing only the dirty blast:

steps.player: I've got you a Greenman's ale, the rotten tomato and the eye of newt, but haven't had any luck on the 'Dirty Blast' yet...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Come back and see me when you've got everything I need!

steps.player: Okay then. I'll get on it.

options.text: Where do I get an eye of newt?

steps.player: Where would I find an eye of newt?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I don't know. A newt's face?

steps.player: Thank you so much for that help.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah, I don't know where they get them, they usually have them at herblore and magic shops.

options.text: Where do I get a rotten tomato?

steps.player: Where would I find a rotten tomato?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'm not entirely sure, but I hear they're sold for public spectacles.

steps.player: Public spectacles?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yeah. Pre-arranged combats, caught thieves on show, that sort of thing.

options.text: Where do I get a greenman's ale?

steps.player: Where would I find a greenman's ale?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, as the official sponsored drink of Castle Wars it might be worth looking around there.

options.text: Where do I get a 'Dirty Blast'?

steps.player: Where would I find a 'Dirty Blast'? I've never heard of it before.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yes, I must admit I had never heard of it either until reading through my ancestor's cookbook.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Tell me, do you know how to make a Fruit Blast?

steps.player: A Fruit Blast? Sure, like they sell at Blurberry's Bar, right?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah, so you've heard of it then? But for this recipe I'd need a fresh one; you can't just buy me one from a shop or from your friends.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, a 'Dirty Blast' is a freshly made Fruit Blast, but then for some reason you add ash at the end!

steps.player: Freshly made? Why did you specify that?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Apparently the ash reacts with the freshly squeezed juice in the glass. It means you can't just buy one Blurberry made earlier, you'll have to make it yourself.

steps.player: Oh. Well, it shouldn't take that long.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: That's the spirit!

steps.player: A Fruit Blast? Can't say I've ever heard of it...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah, well, they're a popular Gnomic delicacy served at the Blurberry bar. But for this recipe I'd need a fresh one; you can't just buy me one from a shop or from your friends.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Basically, what you do is juice a pineapple, an orange and a lemon, then put them all into a cocktail shaker.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Pour that into a glass, then top with a slice of lemon.

steps.player: Okaaaay... So what's a 'Dirty Blast'?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, apparently after you have done the above then by adding ashes you create a unique new drink.

steps.player: Sounds horrible..

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I agree, but it's what the recipe specifically needs.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Bear in mind it will only work with very fresh ingredients, so you will have to make your own cocktail, not rely on one of the pre made ones Blurberry sells.

d-j-vu-using-ashes-on-a-fruit-blast.player: That looks disgusting, but it's what the cook asked for...

d-j-vu-attempting-to-drink-the-dirty-bla.player: No thanks, that looks DISGUSTING! I won't drink that!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.player: About those ingredients you wanted for the banquet...

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.text: Did you bring them? Remember, I need an eye of newt, a glass of greenman's ale, a rotten tomato, and a 'Dirty Blast'!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.player: You will be happy to know... I have all of that with me!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.text: You absolutely MUST go through into the dining room just there and see the feast I have prepared.

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-with-all-of-t.text: I simply won't take no for an answer!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.text: Why haven't you gone and looked at the feast I have prepared yet? Trust me, it will be a sight the likes of which you will never see again!

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.player: I don't know... I'm just... quite busy, I guess...

d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.speaker: Cook
d-j-vu-talking-to-the-cook-again.text: No, honestly, you MUST go in there!

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Screen fades out and in as the player enters the dining hall. Cutscene begins, zooming in on Duke Horacio.
If Beneath Cursed Sands hasn't been completed:

steps.text: Camera switches to Osman.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I welcome Osman, Spymaster for the Emir of Al Kharid.

steps.speaker: Osman
steps.text: I thank you for your hospitality.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: If Beneath Cursed Sands has been completed:

steps.text: Camera switches to Selim.

steps.speaker: Duke Horacio
steps.text: I welcome Selim, acting Spymaster for the Emir of Al Kharid.

steps.speaker: Selim
steps.text: I thank you for your hospitality.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome the chief guard of the White Wolf Mountain dwarves.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome Pirate Pete from Braindeath Island.
Camera switches to Wartface and Bentnoze.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome the chief of the Goblin Village.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome Skrach Uglogwee of the Feldip Hills ogres.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Skrach Uglogwee
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Der ogres, dey call me Bone Cruncher.
Camera switches to the Lumbridge Guide.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I welcome my neighbour, Phileas the Lumbridge Guide.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Lumbridge Guide
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I didn't have far to travel!

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: From the town of Edgeville, I welcome Evil Dave.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Evil Dave
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: These secret meetings are SOOO EVIL!
Camera pans to Sir Amik Varze.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: A hearty welcome to Sir Amik Varze, leader of the White Knights...
Camera switches to an empty chair.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: ...and finally, I welcome the ruler of Ape Atoll, Awowogei.
Horacio kicks Awowogei who moves back several spaces.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Lumbridge Guide
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: I think he's lost his Amulet of Manspeak.
The mysterious old man suddenly teleports next to Horacio, and takes a bow.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Mysterious Old Man
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Here you go Horacio, it's all yours!
The mysterious old man teleports away.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Duke Horacio
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Excuse me while I deal with this...

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Osman/Selim
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: We should do something about that old man.
Evil Bob suddenly teleports next to Osman/Selim.
The door opens and the player walks in.
The Culinaromancer suddenly teleports into the room, at the head of the table.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Culinaromancer
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: Hah! Your chef did! And now I'll kill you!
The Culinaromancer launches a spell at each side of the table. The spells go through every attendee who is seated.
The door opens and Aris walks in.
The Culinaromancer launches a spell at Aris.
Aris conducts a time freezing spell.
The screen flashes white, then fades back in, showing that all the attendees except Aris and the player have been frozen in time.

chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.speaker: Aris
chef-surprise-the-lumbridge-secret-counc.text: [player name], you must help me defeat this evil!
Screen fades to black as cutscene ends.

chef-surprise-talking-to-aris.speaker: Aris
chef-surprise-talking-to-aris.text: Hello there adventurer. How can I assist you?

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I am the fortune-teller. My friends call me Aris.

steps.player: Okay then Aris...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Was there something you wanted to ask me about?

steps.player: I do have a question. A very GOOD question.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Oh yes? What's that then?

steps.player: Just what in the flipping hippo is going on?!?!?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: ...flipping hippo?

steps.player: Yeeeess.... You've never heard that phrase?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: No, no I'm quite sure that I never have.

steps.player: Well, that's not the point!
Please, tell me what just happened!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Certainly. That fellow over there in the chef's hat is called the Culinaromancer.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: A hundred years ago, he threatened the secret council with death, but was foiled by the quick thinking of his assistant, who managed to trap him in another dimension.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: As a result of that action, the assistant was offered a job for life as head cook of Lumbridge, for himself and all his future descendants.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Now, apparently the current head cook of Lumbridge decided to recreate his ancestors greatest achievement, not realising that his achievement was not a meal but a powerful food-magic, and by recreating the spell he has

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: inadvertently freed the evil Culinaromancer from his prison, to wreak havoc upon this world once more.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Naturally, when I saw what was happening, I intervened with a simple Tempus Cessit spell, so that we would have time to immunise the secret council from his attack, and so that we can defeat the Culinaromancer

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: once and for all.

steps.player: Um... what?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: You want me to explain it again?

steps.player: Yes please. But slower. And more understandable.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: (sigh) Okay then: 100 years ago, the evil food magician was defeated and banished.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Because of you and the Lumbridge cook, he is now free.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: He was about to slaughter all of these people, but I stopped time so that you could protect them.

steps.player: You stopped time? And... wait, I have to protect them? Why me?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes I stopped time. And YOU have to do it partly because you helped release him by getting those ingredients, and partly because I am stuck here keeping the spell intact.

steps.player: Isn't stopping time kind of... You know, dangerous?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Oh, unbelievably so. This is why I have limited the time bubble to this room and this room alone.

steps.player: Huh? How does that work?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Everything outside this room continues to flow through time. This is why outside of this room you have already defeated the Culinaromancer, and protected the

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: members of the secret council.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Inside this room however you have not.

steps.player: Uh... what?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Where time has been frozen in this room, outside it continues to flow, so this room is now currently in what we would call 'the past', meaning events inside here have already happened, and the longer time continues to flow

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: outside, the more removed from normal time this room becomes.

steps.player: Wait... so I've already saved all of these council members and defeated the Culinaromancer?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. But only outside. What you need to do now is save them in here as well, so that time can resume its normal ebb and flow.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Otherwise there will be increasing temporal pressure, and the entire universe might explode!

steps.player: Not the whole universe! That's where I keep my stuff!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. That is why it is so important that you protect them all.

steps.player: But... You said I already had...?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. You have. In the future, which is also the present, but not in the present, which is also the past.

steps.player: My brain hurts...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, time travel tends to do that to people.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I suggest you don't worry about it too much, just make sure you protect each council member and then defeat the Culinaromancer.

steps.player: How would I do that?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Each council member will have their own unique dish that will serve to counteract the Culinaromancer's spell.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Inspect the one you wish to save, and I will offer any advice I have.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Was there anything else you wanted to ask me about?

steps.player: Who's that guy over there? Seemed like you knew each other.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: He calls himself the Culinaromancer. He is an extremely evil man, with incredibly powerful magics.

steps.player: Culinaromancer?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, that's correct. Just as an Oneiromancer draws their magical powers from dreams, or a  necromancer draws their strength from the energies of the dead, a Culinaromancer uses

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: food as his source of magical power.

steps.player: Food? What's so dangerous about food?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Do not underestimate the latent power of foodstuffs as a source of magical energy.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Not only are they a fundamental life-force, but they often evoke great emotional attachment.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Do not underestimate him, part of his strength lies in the fact his unique type of magical power is quite obscure, I have seen many fall before him.

steps.player: Okay, so he's powerful, but I don't get why he's here!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ah, it is a very old story indeed.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: A hundred years ago, he worked here in Lumbridge castle for the then Duke as a cook.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: This was all a pretence, of course. As part of his duties he was allowed access to many exotic and esoteric foodstuffs. These allowed him to experiment with his magic and increase his power exponentially.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Building his power was just the first step however.

steps.player: How do you mean?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Knowing of the regular meetings of the secret council here in Lumbridge, the Culinaromancer decided that he would eliminate all of them as the first step to his plans for world domination.

steps.player: Would that have worked?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Possibly, we might never know. As his plans were coming to fruition his assistant discovered them, and used his own magic against him, to trap him in another dimension where his powers would

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: be useless.

steps.player: Then how did he escape?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Well, the current cook of Lumbridge obviously discovered an ancient manuscript of his ancestors, and believing it to be a recipe decided to recreate the spell that banished him.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Which obviously seems to have opened the portal enough for him to escape back to this dimension. So this is partly your fault.

steps.player: Oh. Those ingredients?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, those ingredients. So I hold you responsible for assisting me in ridding him of this dimension once and for all.

steps.player: Yeah... I had a feeling you were going to say that...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Are you clear on what you have to do, or was there something you wished me to explain?

steps.player: Who are these people? Seems like quite the random selection in here!

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: The people you see assembled here are the self-styled secret council of Gielinor.

steps.player: 'Self-styled' council? What do you mean?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Many centuries ago, a small group from around the world of Gielinor decided that these lands needed to be directed, that it was too risky to leave the fates of this land to luck and the gods.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: They decided that every 10 years they would meet to discuss current events, and shape how the world might then develop.

steps.player: So they're pretty influential people?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: No, not really. For all of their grand schemes and ideas, nothing ever gets done except every ten years they have a bit of a posh meal together and a bit of a gossip.

steps.player: I see... But this evil cook guy that just appeared thinks they might be important?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: I don't really know what he thinks.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Either way I'm not prepared to let him get away with a brazen attack on anybody while I have the power to stop him.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: And given that this is partly your fault, I fully expect your assistance in saving them.

steps.player: MY fault??

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. You were the one who provided the cook with the ingredients that he needed to allow the Culinaromancer to return to this dimension.

steps.player: I just don't understand any of this...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: What exactly is it that you don't understand?

steps.player: Uh... Is it me, or did this room just get much bigger?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ah, that would be the time dilation effect.

steps.player: The... time dilation... effect?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes. As time has stopped flowing in the normal way, your eyes are playing tricks on you, as the pictures absorbed by your eyes take slightly longer to reach your brain

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: than normal.

steps.player: Erm... what?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: As everybody knows, time flows from north to south, so my freezing time means that this room has apparently stretched slightly along its horizontal axis.

steps.player: Um... does that even make sense?

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Don't let it worry you too much. It's just an optical illusion, the room is exactly the same size as it always has been, it just appears to be a tiny bit bigger.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Anything else you wanted to know?

steps.player: Ah, forget it, I don't want to talk to you now.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Yes, I'm sure you have far more important things to do than SAVING THE ENTIRE UNIVERSE!

chef-surprise-talking-to-aris-in-varrock.text: If the player has not started or is in the middle of Demon Slayer:

steps.prompt: What do you wish to ask about?

chef-surprise-talking-to-aris-in-varrock.text: If the player has completed Demon Slayer:

steps.player: Fancy seeing you here again.

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Don't talk to me! It might cause a time paradox!

steps.player: Huh? But how can it when you're...

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: LA-LA-LA I'M NOT TALKING TO YOU LA-LA-LA TIME PARADOX LA-LA-LA

steps.player: Uh... Okay then.

recipe-for-success.player: Can we talk about what happened in the dining room?

recipe-for-success.speaker: Cook
recipe-for-success.text: Wow! You were incredible! The way you defeated the Culinaromancer, you made it seem so easy!
When talking to the cook for the first time:

steps.player: Uh... What?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: With the foods, and that big portal thingy, and everything!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'm just glad you were around, who knows WHAT could have happened if you weren't able to help us!

steps.player: I'm sorry, I don't have any clue what you...
Oh. Oh, right. This must be part of that whole time-bubble thing that Aris told me about.
So the cook outside of the bubble remembers me having already saved the council members even though I haven't actually gone and done it yet...
Gah! This time travel stuff makes my head hurt!

recipe-for-success.player: So... I don't suppose you can remember exactly how I defeated him can you?

recipe-for-success.speaker: Cook
recipe-for-success.text: Of course! Which bit can't you remember doing?

steps.player: That dwarf... I somehow can't remember how I managed to save him...

steps.text: If the player has not inspected the mountain dwarf:
If the player has inspected the mountain dwarf:

steps.player: That dwarf... I somehow can't remember how I managed to save him...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: The dwarf? Oh, yeah, I think that was an easy one, didn't you say?

steps.player: I did? Er, I did.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: You went to see his dad in the tunnels under white wolf mountain, and then got some rock cakes, if I remember rightly.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

steps.player: Those bickering goblins... How did I protect them again?

steps.text: If the player has not inspected the goblin generals:

steps.speaker: Aris
steps.text: Ask me how to protect them first, otherwise you will cause a time paradox! I'm keeping an eye on you, you know!
If the player has inspected the goblin generals:

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, that was a weird one alright, you told me that they couldn't agree on what food they liked, so you ended up just mushing a bunch of stuff together somehow which seemed to do the trick.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

steps.player: I can't quite remember how I managed to save that pirate...

steps.text: If the player has not inspected Pirate Pete:
If the player has inspected Pirate Pete:

steps.player: I can't quite remember how I managed to save that pirate...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: The pirate? Yes, you used fishcakes didn't you?

steps.player: I did? Er... I mean I did.
Out of interest, could you just help me quickly with that?
Can you tell me how to make fishcakes?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Fishcakes? As in with fish eggs and fish milk?

steps.player: Don't be silly, that would never work.
Can you check to see if there is a recipe for them?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Of course.
The Chef checks one of his cookbooks.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Found it!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Apparently you need Ground Cod, Ground Kelp, Ground Giant Crab Meat and Breadcrumbs.

options.text: Where do I get Ground Cod?

steps.player: Where do I get Ground Cod?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, if you use a pestle and mortar on a raw cod that will grind it up nicely.

options.text: Where do I get Ground Kelp?

steps.player: Where do I get Ground kelp?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: There are apparently some kelp patches off the coast near Rimmington. Murphy knows more about that.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: As for the grinding part, all you have to do is use a pestle and mortar on it, that ought to get it sorted.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Murphy also used to bring in Giant Crabs occasionally. He hasn't had any of them in for a while though.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: You had best go and have a word with him to see if he can tell you what happened.

options.text: Where do I get Ground Giant Crab Meat?

steps.player: Where do I get Ground Giant Crab meat?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, Murphy used to bring in Giant Crabs occasionally. He hasn't had any of them in for a while though.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: You had best go and have a word with him to see if he can tell you what happened.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh, and  there are apparently some kelp patches off the coast near Rimmington. Murphy knows about that too.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: As for the grinding part, all you have to do is use a pestle and mortar on it, that ought to get it sorted.

steps.player: Where do I get Breadcrumbs?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: That's easy, all you do is use a knife to slice the bread up into tiny, tiny chunks.

options.text: What do I do with all of it?

steps.player: What did I do with all of it?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'm not entirely sure. What am I, an encyclopedia?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I'll have a look through my cookbook while I wait for the ingredients.

steps.player: Ok, I'll go out and get all of the stuff and bring it to you.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ok.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Is there anything else you need to know?

options.condition: If the player has asked at least one question

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: No problem!

steps.player: The Lumbridge guide... I can't really rememember what I did to save him...

steps.text: If the player has not inspected the Lumbridge Guide:
If the player has inspected the Lumbridge Guide:

steps.player: The Lumbridge guide... I can't really rememember what I did to save him...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh, you told me that that crazy wizard in the wizards' tower helped you with that.

steps.player: That crazy wizard at the wizards' tower? Was I not any more specific than that?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: No, not really. I think you might have mentioned the name Traiborn though.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

steps.player: That fellow with the unhealthy obsession with black... Dave his name is...
I can't quite remember what I did to protect him...

steps.text: If the player has not inspected Evil Dave:
If the player has inspected Evil Dave:

steps.player: That fellow with the unhealthy obsession with black... Dave his name is...
I can't quite remember what I did to protect him...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh yeah! I didn't understand that one myself, but apparently you went and asked him how he likes his stew, then made him remember it after he'd tasted it!

steps.player: Uh... what?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yeah, I didn't understand it either, but you mentioned something about demonic incursions and evil cats too!

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

steps.player: Just remind me again how I managed to unfreeze Skrach?

steps.text: If the player has not inspected Skrach Uglogwee:
If the player has inspected Skrach Uglogwee:

steps.player: Just remind me again how I managed to unfreeze Skrach?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Certainly. Everyone knows that Skrach loves Jubbly Chompy, preferably roasted on a spit! The bird's carcass is so big, it can't be cooked any other way.

steps.player: And how do I get one of those?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: I wouldn't know much about that, but I believe you talked to Rantz quite a bit over in the Feldip hills. Apparently, he got you to do him quite a few favours before you actually got the Jubbly.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

steps.player: That white knight... Sir Amik Varze... I can't quite remember how I saved him...

steps.text: If the player has not inspected Sir Amik Varze:
If the player has inspected Sir Amik Varze:

steps.player: but it was something to do with creme brulee supreme...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Ah yes! Why, I was so impressed with that recipe you created that I memorised it!

steps.player: Ah, you did, did you? I don't suppose you could refresh my memory about that?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: But of course! It was an unusual dish, an unusual dish indeed! First you blend together, in a pot, some milk and some cream. Then add cornflour to the mixture.

steps.player: Cornflour? How do I... er, how DID I make that then?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh, you told me you used sweetcorn in a mill!

steps.player: Really? Weird. Okay, what did I do then?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Then you travelled to the Kharazi Jungle and searched the plants there until you found a vanilla stick, which was then added to the mixture.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: After that you told me that you sought out and killed the fearsome Evil Chicken, to get one of his eggs, which was then mixed with the other ingredients.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Finally you made some cinnamon by grinding the branch of a Dramen Tree and sprinkled it on top of the creme brulee.

steps.player: Sounds easy enough so far. Er, I mean it was easy enough up to that point.

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Yes, but then came the impressive part!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Apparently, a creme brulee supreme needs to be flambed at exactly the right temperature, and the only fire that is hot enough to do this is the breath of a dragon. Luckily, while killing black dragons near the Evil

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Chicken's lair, you came across a method of forcing a dragon to your will so that it would complete the dish, which you then used to protect Sir Amik!

steps.player: I definitely said that I had to kill some black dragons to do that?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh yes. You were quite adamant about it. Specifically black dragons. Specifically near the Evil Chicken's lair.

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

steps.player: The monkey king... However did I save him from the culinaromancer...?

steps.text: If the player has not inspected King Awowogei:
If the player has inspected King Awowogei:

steps.player: The monkey king... However did I save him from the culinaromancer...?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Well, it was something that sounded ABSOLUTELY DISGUSTING that you picked up on Ape Atoll...

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Oh MAN! That was AWESOME!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: After you managed to save all of the members of the secret council with those weird foods, the culinaromancer tried to make a run for it, but you followed him into his magic portal and Biff! Bang! Boom!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: sorted him out once and for all!

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you ever know that you're my hero?

steps.player: Oh yeah... I remember now...

steps.speaker: Cook
steps.text: Did you want a reminder on any other of your brave exploits?
